title: Finite subfamilies of completely decomposed etale covers over a Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a scheme admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $I$ be a set and let $(u_i:U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be a family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose that for every $x\in X$ there are $i\in I$ and $z\in U_i$ with $u_i(z)=x$ and induced residue-field map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(z)$ an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]. Then there is a finite subset $I_0\subseteq I$ such that the same property holds with $i\in I_0$. No quasi-compactness, separation or finiteness assumption on the individual $U_i$ is required.

source.place: Expose II, Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27, completely decomposed case ell=infinity, using Proposition 2.2.3 and compactness of the constructible topology.

proof.text: The finite affine Noetherian cover in the hypothesis is a locally Noetherian cover in [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. This gives the descending-chain condition on closed subsets: an infinite strictly descending chain would be a nonempty family with no minimal member. Thus [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] makes every subset of $X$, in particular every open, quasi-compact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] and then [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral] to see that $X$ is spectral. Its constructible topology is therefore quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-topology-quasi-compact].

source.place: Expose II, Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27, completely decomposed case ell=infinity, using Proposition 2.2.3 and compactness of the constructible topology.

proof.text: For each $i\in I$, define $C_i=\{x\in X:\exists z\in U_i,\ u_i(z)=x,\ \kappa(x)\to\kappa(z)\text{ is an isomorphism}\}$. An etale morphism is locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The finite-polynomial presentation in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] is in particular finitely generated, so it is locally of finite type in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $x\in C_i$, apply [lem-per-rational-lift-locally-closed-section] to $u_i$ to obtain a locally closed subscheme $j:Z\hookrightarrow X$ through $x$ and $s:Z\to U_i$ with $u_i\circ s=j$.

source.place: Expose II, Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27, completely decomposed case ell=infinity, using Proposition 2.2.3 and compactness of the constructible topology.

proof.text: The image $j(Z)$ is contained in $C_i$. Indeed, an immersion induces residue-field isomorphisms: for a closed immersion this is the equality of the residue fields of $A$ at a prime containing an ideal $J$ and of $A/J$ at the corresponding prime, and for an open immersion the local rings agree. These affine descriptions are in [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. For $t\in Z$, put $w=j(t)$ and $z=s(t)$. On residue fields [def-weil-residue-field], the composite $\kappa(w)\xrightarrow{a}\kappa(z)\xrightarrow{b}\kappa(t)$ is the isomorphism induced by $j$. Identifying the last field with the first gives $ba=1$. Every unital field homomorphism is injective; hence $b(a(b(v)))=b(v)$ implies $a(b(v))=v$ for each $v\in\kappa(z)$. Thus $a$ is an isomorphism, proving $w\in C_i$.

source.place: Expose II, Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27, completely decomposed case ell=infinity, using Proposition 2.2.3 and compactness of the constructible topology.

proof.text: Write the locally closed image as $j(Z)=O\cap F$ with $O$ open and $F$ closed, using the closed-then-open factorization of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. By Step 1 both $O$ and $X\setminus F$ are quasi-compact opens. The subbase definition [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology] makes $O$ and $F$ open in the constructible topology, so $j(Z)$ is open there. Steps 2--3 give such a subset through every $x\in C_i$, contained in $C_i$. Therefore each $C_i$ is a union of open subsets in that topology and is open there.

source.place: Expose II, Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27, completely decomposed case ell=infinity, using Proposition 2.2.3 and compactness of the constructible topology.

proof.text: The covering hypothesis is exactly $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}C_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-constructible-topology-quasi-compact] applied to the open cover from Step 4, choose a finite subset $I_0\subseteq I$ with $X=\bigcup_{i\in I_0}C_i$. Unfolding $C_i$ gives every required residue-field-isomorphism lift with its index in $I_0$. When $X$ is empty the empty subset suffices; when $X$ is nonempty the hypothesis excludes an empty $I$. The proof never requires the individual $U_i$ to be quasi-compact or separated.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q11-8349315f4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read ILO II 2.1.1 and 2.2.1–2.2.4 (printed pp. 26–27). The item is exactly the ℓ=∞ case of Corollary 2.2.4, with no extra hypotheses on the U_i. The new node lem-per-rational-lift-locally-closed-section is Proposition 2.2.3, with 'subscheme' made precise as an immersion. It is statement-only, introduces every object it uses, and has the correct blueprint from/via/same_as. It is not a restatement of the item: it is pointwise and has no family or compactness. It is not a duplicate: I grepped for Nisnevich, completely decomposed, 2.2.3, section on a locally closed subscheme and the spreading-out tags. The nearest node, lem-sbc-pointed-section-stage-descent, is a general limit tool, not this statement. I tested it on: a closed point of Spec Z, the generic point with the open D(2), Spec Z[i] (no rational lift, no section), nonreduced Spec k[ε] (needs a subscheme, not an open), and the reverse direction via the field argument. Steps: (1) The cited statements check out: locnoeth, minimal closed subsets, DCC compactness, 01OY, 094L, and 0901 for spectral spaces. Quasi-compactness from the finite cover is implicit (advisory). (2) Étale gives lfp, which gives lft. The locality in def-weil-finite-type-morphism is one routine 01T2-style sentence (advisory). (3) Immersions induce residue-field isomorphisms; with ba an isomorphism and b injective, a is an isomorphism. Correct. (4) j(Z)=O∩F is open in the constructible topology because every open is quasi-compact (Step 1). Correct. (5) Compactness gives a finite I_0; the empty X case is handled. The citers (finite-flat-cd-etale-exchange step 7, uniformization-nodal-quotient-reduction) use the unchanged statement. No SGA source, no cycle, no tool_uses needed. No fixes.
